purpose: How a working gold-plating bench turns a mechanically finished piece into a chemically clean, activated, tank-ready surface: sequencing soak and ultrasonic degrease, electroclean polarity choice, the water-break gate, pickle and activation keyed to the verified substrate class, rinse cascade and water quality, no-touch handling, and the time-boxed transfer into the tank, so adhesion is decided correctly before any gold is spent.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the context is a bench-scale jewelry plating line: small heated tanks, racked or wired piecework, one operator, not an industrial reel-to-reel installation
every cleaner, electrocleaner, pickle and activation product on the line is a purchased commercial product with its technical data sheet and safety data sheet on file; the TDS governs setpoints
upstream triage (substrate identity, stones, repairs, sign-off) and mechanical finishing are complete before a piece reaches this line; this KB consumes their outputs and never redoes them

workplace, hazmat, and discharge rules are jurisdiction-specific obligation classes; the shop verifies its own jurisdiction's current rules and this content stays educational, never personalized legal or medical advice
exclusions: substrate identification and piece triage: base-metal families, hallmark reading, magnet/weight/spot-test method classes, accept/refuse/refer decisions and irreversibility sign-off are the assessment KB's territory; this line runs only on a signed triage docket it did not create

mechanical finishing before plate: buffing, compound selection, wheel versus tumble decisions, scratch and pit removal, and the target pre-plate finish are the mechanical-finishing KB's territory; this KB removes compound residue but never chooses or re-cuts a finish
stone-set, pearl or organic, antique, filled or repaired pieces: these are triaged for refusal, stone removal, or referral before any chemistry, and never enter the wet line to keep a job

plating bath operation: live-entry strike execution, underplate and gold bath chemistry, current control and deposit quality belong to the plating benches downstream; this KB ends at correct, timely tank entry
improvised chemistry: no DIY bath formulation from raw chemicals, no mixing regimes a TDS does not sanction, and absolute cyanide/acid segregation wherever both exist on a line

asserted universal setpoints: temperatures, concentrations, times, current densities and conductivity thresholds appear only as mechanisms, TDS-governed values, or explicitly labeled handbook-class ranges, never as invented universal fact
jurisdictional numeric limits for waste, discharge, or exposure stated as fact: these are named obligation classes with the instruction to verify current local rules

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREP_CHAIN_MISSION explains the soil-class ladder and why adhesion is decided pre-tank; ADHESION_FAILURE_DIAGNOSIS maps each failure signature back to its prep step

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRIAGE_INTAKE_GATE states the signed-docket rule and the flag classes that keep a piece off the line; RACKING_CONTACT covers the racked, contact-verified physical state

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOAK_DEGREASE gives the saponification/emulsification mechanism for bulk compound removal and ULTRASONIC_DEGREASE gives cavitation for recesses, each with its named failure territory

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ELECTROCLEAN_MECHANISM explains gas-scrubbing at the work surface, why anodic avoids smut plate-out and hydrogen charging on steel, and the anodic time limits on tarnish-prone copper alloys

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACTIVATION_DIP_TIMING explains flash-oxide reset after rinsing, the dip's role as a sacrificial contamination buffer, and why immediacy before transfer is the entire point

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RINSE_CASCADE_DESIGN gives counterflow staging and the dead rinse; RINSE_WATER_QUALITY assigns tap-grade early stages and DI final stages with the conductivity pen as the control instrument

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTERTANK_DRAG_CONTROL names the alkaline-into-pickle, silicate-gel, and chloride/nickel-into-gold routes with drain-time and rinse countermeasures

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NO_TOUCH_HANDLING states the rack-and-tool-only rule, why a fingerprint restarts the chain at soak, and that a wipe never substitutes for re-cleaning

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSFER_CLOCK gives the wet-and-fast rule, flash rust and repassivation as the blown-clock evidence per substrate, and re-activation (never proceeding) as the recovery

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BATH_LIFE_MAINTENANCE gives TDS-anchored life tracking, the cleaning-time-doubles and performance-collapse dump signals, and spent solutions as jurisdiction-verified waste classes; TDS_CHEMISTRY_DISCIPLINE anchors the governing documents

competency_questions.question: What is the operational definition of plate-ready, and what recorded evidence releases a piece from the prep line into a tank?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLATE_READY_RELEASE lists the release conditions - water-break pass on record, substrate-correct activation, live transfer clock, unbroken no-touch chain - and the release record that carries them

glossary.definition: The bench's free, instant, binary cleanliness gate: a piece withdrawn from clean rinse water must hold an unbroken sheeting film over its whole surface (shop practice reads it over roughly half a minute); any beading or pull-back reveals remaining organic soil and fails the piece backward to degrease.

Solution carried on the work, rack, and trapped recesses from one tank into the next, where it contaminates the receiving chemistry - alkaline cleaner neutralizing a pickle, or chloride and nickel ions poisoning a gold bath.

Process solution carried out of its own tank on the work and rack; on prep tanks it is a contamination and waste stream, and just before a gold tank it is recoverable metal value a dead rinse exists to capture.

Electrocleaning with the workpiece wired positive so oxygen evolves at its surface and gas-scrubs the last soil monolayer; the standard mode for steel because it avoids the smut plate-out and hydrogen charging that cathodic operation causes.

The thin self-healing oxide (chromium oxide on stainless, an aged oxide on old nickel plate) that re-forms in seconds in air and water and prevents metallic bonding; it must be removed and covered in essentially the same instant, which ordinary dips cannot do.

The final chemical depassivation of a cleaned surface - dissolving flash oxide so bare active metal, not oxide, meets the first deposit; its chemistry class is keyed to the substrate class and its value decays from the moment it is done.

Two or more rinse tanks plumbed or worked so the piece moves toward ever-cleaner water while make-up water flows the opposite way; standard rinse-ratio math makes a cascade dramatically more water-efficient than one big overflowing rinse.

A static, unplumbed rinse tank placed before a critical or precious bath; it accumulates what the work carries and acts as a sacrificial buffer, and ahead of gold it doubles as the recovery vessel for dragged-out metal.

The visible orange bloom that forms on activated steel within around a minute of air exposure between tanks; it is the substrate announcing the transfer clock is blown and the piece must be re-activated, not plated over.

The supplier document that governs a commercial prep product's make-up, operating window, control tests, and maintenance; on this line the TDS outranks bench habit, and a regime the TDS does not sanction is not run.

nodes.definition: Hold the whole prep line to its governing logic: electrodeposits bond only to chemically clean, oxide-free, active metal, and the chain removes three soil classes in a fixed order - organic soil (buffing compound, skin oils, shop grease) by alkaline saponification and emulsification, then inorganic oxide and tarnish by acid, then the passive film on substrates that re-form one. Order is not decorative: acid over oil pits the metal under the soil instead of cleaning it, and activating a surface that still carries organics locks the contamination under the deposit. This node is why nearly every peeling, blistering, or sheeting-off gold job traces to a prep step and not to the gold bath, and it gives the operator the mental model to place every tank, gate, and clock on the line.

included: the claim that adhesion is decided pre-tank

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a documented adhesion failure whose root cause sits outside the three-soil-class model, or process references that reorder the chain for a substrate this shop runs

pros.claim: One ladder explains and orders every station on the line, so a new operator can reason instead of memorize
pros.example: seeing beading water after electroclean, the operator knows the failure is organic-class and returns to soak rather than reaching for a stronger pickle

cons.claim: The ladder tempts over-generalization across substrates that do not share it cleanly
cons.example: zinc die-cast has almost no tolerance for the acid rungs, so running the full ladder as written destroys the piece the model was meant to protect

failure_modes: treating the gold bath as the suspect for adhesion failures and dumping good chemistry while the soak cleaner stays exhausted
running acid steps over organic soil and pitting the substrate under the grease
skipping a rung on a rush job because the piece already looks clean
acceptance_tests: the operator can name the three soil classes, the removal mechanism for each, and what goes wrong when any two are swapped in order
revisit_triggers: a failure analysis shows an adhesion loss the soil-class ladder cannot explain
a new substrate class or coating enters the shop whose soils do not fit the three-class model

nodes.definition: Enforce the line's entry rule: no piece touches wet chemistry without the signed triage docket from the assessment bench stating the verified substrate class (established by test-method classes - magnet, weight and feel, hallmark reading, spot test - never assumed from appearance), the flag status for stones, pearls and organics, solder joints, filled or repaired zones, antique or sentimental status, and any customer sign-off already obtained for irreversible work. This node does not perform triage - it consumes it, checks it is complete and current for the piece actually in hand, and turns away anything flagged or undocumented. The prep line's authority here is refusal only: a mismatch between docket and piece goes back to assessment, never gets resolved by the plater's own guess.

excluded: performing substrate tests or hallmark reading

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an incident review showing the docket fields fail to capture a hazard class the wet line actually meets, or the assessment bench changes its docket format

pros.claim: A hard paper gate makes the sibling boundary physical, so no customer piece is risked to keep a job moving
pros.example: a ring arrives with a foiled-back garnet nobody mentioned; the docket has no stone flag, so the line refuses it back to assessment instead of soaking the foil off in hot cleaner

cons.claim: On a one-person bench the gate feels like bureaucracy and gets skipped exactly when the shop is busiest
cons.example: a rush chain job goes straight into the ultrasonic without a docket and a hidden lead-solder repair joint lets go in the tank

failure_modes: running a piece on a stale docket after the customer swapped items at the counter
the plater re-doing a spot test at the wet bench and quietly overriding the assessment call
treating an obvious-looking substrate as verified because it looks like brass
acceptance_tests: every piece on the line can be matched to a docket naming substrate class, flag status, and sign-off state before its first immersion
a deliberately flagged test docket is refused at the gate rather than worked
revisit_triggers: any wet-line incident involving a stone, repair, or misidentified substrate that a docket should have caught

nodes.definition: Bind every solution on the prep line to a purchased commercial product run inside its technical data sheet: make-up per the TDS, operating window per the TDS, control tests and replenishment per the TDS, and no mixing regime the TDS does not sanction. The discipline has three working parts: a TDS and SDS on file and physically findable for every tank; setpoints transcribed from the sheet into the bench log rather than remembered; and a standing rule that when bench habit and the sheet disagree, the sheet wins, and when the sheet is silent, the supplier gets a question before the tank gets an experiment. Handbook-class ranges from published plating literature may inform expectations, but they are referenced as ranges - the specific product's sheet governs the specific tank.

excluded: formulating any bath from raw chemicals
inventing numeric setpoints the sheet does not state

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a TDS revision, product substitution, or supplier guidance that changes any transcribed setpoint or control test on the line

pros.claim: TDS anchoring makes results reproducible across days and operators and gives every dispute a written referee
pros.example: when the electrocleaner underperforms, the bench titrates against the TDS control test instead of arguing about whether it feels weak

cons.claim: Sheets are written for industrial volumes and sometimes leave a bench-scale question genuinely open
cons.example: a TDS assumes continuous filtration a two-liter bench tank does not have, so the shop must ask the supplier how life tracking changes at small volume

failure_modes: running a cleaner from memory of a previous brand's sheet after switching suppliers
topping up a tank by eye until its composition is unknown
adopting an internet recipe to stretch a product beyond its sheet
acceptance_tests: every tank on the line can be traced to a named commercial product, its on-file TDS, and a log entry showing make-up per that sheet
revisit_triggers: a supplier revises a TDS or a product is discontinued and substituted
any observed tank behavior the on-file sheet does not predict

nodes.definition: Hold the one line on the bench that is never negotiated: where cyanide-bearing products and acids both exist in a shop, they are never mixed, never stored together, and never share a drain, because acid contact with cyanide liberates hydrogen cyanide gas, which is fatal. The obligation classes this node owns are physical segregation (separate storage, separate spill paths, separate rinse and waste streams), labeling every vessel including rinses, PPE and eyewash placement, ventilation over the tanks, formal training before anyone works the line, and emergency readiness - all with the standing instruction to verify the current workplace and hazmat rules of the shop's own jurisdiction. The bench-scale escape hatch is first-class content: a small shop can usually choose cyanide-free prep products and delete the hazard class entirely, and that choice outranks any process convenience.

included: segregation, storage, labeling, drain-separation obligation classes
excluded: jurisdiction-specific numeric exposure or discharge limits stated as fact
medical advice beyond routing exposure concerns to professional care

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: introduction or removal of any cyanide-bearing product on site, a layout change, or updated jurisdictional hazmat guidance affecting storage and drains

pros.claim: An absolute rule survives stress, fatigue, and staff turnover in a way a judgment call never does
pros.example: because the acid line and the alkaline-cyanide products have separate labeled sinks, a tired operator physically cannot pour a spent pickle into the wrong drain

cons.claim: Full segregation costs bench space and duplicate vessels a small shop feels acutely
cons.example: a one-room studio must give up a second sink and separate storage cabinet, which is exactly why the cyanide-free product route is usually the better bench-scale answer

failure_modes: a shared rinse bucket quietly bridging the two chemistries
an unlabeled spray bottle of acid dip migrating to the cleaner shelf
assuming a borrowed or inherited product is cyanide-free without reading its SDS
acceptance_tests: a walk of the line shows separate storage, separate labeled drains and rinse vessels, and no path a spill or a pour can take from acid to cyanide
every product's SDS has been checked for cyanide content and the finding is recorded
revisit_triggers: any new product, tank, or layout change on the line
a change in the shop's jurisdictional workplace or hazmat rules

nodes.definition: Run the heated alkaline soak that does the bulk organic removal: saponifiable oils and the wax-and-grease binder of buffing compound are split by alkalinity while the surfactant package emulsifies and lifts what will not saponify. On a jewelry bench the dominant soil is polishing compound packed into recesses by the finishing bench, plus skin oils from handling, and the working variables the TDS governs are concentration, temperature, and time - heat does much of the work, and a soak that is cold or depleted simply relocates grease instead of removing it. Silicated cleaners earn a specific caution: their residue polymerizes in the downstream acid if rinsing is skimpy, showing up much later as a paint-like peel. Oil-splitting products that let soil separate for skimming outlast emulsifying ones in a small tank, a difference the TDS and the bench log make visible.

included: bulk organic and compound removal by heated alkaline chemistry

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a compound-family change upstream, a cleaner product change, or logged soak times drifting against the TDS control test

pros.claim: A well-run soak removes the heavy soil load cheaply so the later, more sensitive stations only polish the cleanliness
pros.example: rouge-caked filigree that would exhaust an electrocleaner in minutes comes out of a hot soak visually free of compound before it ever sees current

cons.claim: The soak's very effectiveness hides its own decline, because it keeps looking busy after it stops working
cons.example: a tank that has quietly doubled its required cleaning time still foams and smells like cleaner, and the failure only surfaces at the water-break gate

failure_modes: cold or under-strength soak smearing compound instead of lifting it
silicate residue carried into the pickle and gelling
extending soak time indefinitely instead of reading it as a dump signal
acceptance_tests: after the soak stage, no visible compound remains in recesses under a loupe and the piece proceeds without acid contact having touched organic soil
revisit_triggers: the finishing bench changes compound family and the soak stops lifting it in normal time

nodes.definition: Use the ultrasonic tank for what immersion alone cannot reach: cavitation collapse scrubs compound and soil out of crevices, chain links, under gallery work, behind filigree, and inside hollow forms, and it does its real work in warm alkaline cleaner, not plain water. The unit's frequency and the bath it runs are equipment- and TDS-governed; the bench judgment this node owns is coverage and restraint - rotating the load so shadowed recesses see cavitation, and recognizing construction that cavitation can damage. Because stone-set, pearl, filled, and repaired pieces are excluded upstream, the residual risk sits in what a docket can miss: hollow soldered constructions, thin previous plate already lifting at an edge, and enamel. When the ultrasonic finds such a weakness the correct reading is that triage missed a flag, and the piece goes back, not onward.

included: cavitation cleaning of recesses and hollow geometry
excluded: clearing stone-set or pearl pieces for ultrasonic exposure (they never reach this line)
using the ultrasonic as a substitute for a depleted soak

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: equipment change (frequency, tank size), a cleaner change altering cavitation behavior, or an incident showing a construction class the current caution list misses

pros.claim: Cavitation is the only practical way to degrease geometry a brush or soak cannot enter
pros.example: a curb chain packed with tripoli through every link comes clean in minutes where any hand method would leave the water-break gate failing at each link shadow

cons.claim: The same energy that strips compound attacks weak joints and lifting films
cons.example: an old repair with a starved solder seam opens up in the ultrasonic, turning a cleaning step into a customer-piece incident that triage sign-off should have priced in

failure_modes: running the unit with plain water and mistaking agitation for cleaning
leaving a dense load stacked so shadowed surfaces never see cavitation
continuing the cycle after hearing a rattle that is a piece shedding a component
acceptance_tests: loupe inspection of the worst recess on the load shows no residual compound after the ultrasonic pass
revisit_triggers: any piece damage plausibly attributable to cavitation, which also triggers a docket-fields review with the assessment bench

nodes.definition: Run electrocleaning as the last-monolayer step and choose polarity by mechanism, not habit. Current through the hot alkaline electrocleaner evolves gas at the workpiece - oxygen when the work is anodic, hydrogen at roughly twice the volume when cathodic - and that gas physically scrubs off the final soil film no soak removes. Anodic is the standard for steel because cathodic operation plates dissolved metal and smut back onto the work and charges the substrate with hydrogen; anodic instead very slightly dissolves the work surface, carrying the last contamination away with it. On tarnish-prone copper alloys and nickel silver, anodic time is kept short because extended anodic exposure oxidizes and dulls the surface the finishing bench just made; where a supplier sheet sanctions a cathodic or periodic-reverse cycle for such work, the sheet's regime governs. Voltage, current density, temperature, and time live in the TDS; the polarity decision and its reasons live here.

included: polarity choice per substrate class and its mechanism
anodic time restraint on tarnish-prone alloys
excluded: numeric setpoints beyond the product TDS
electrocleaning as a substitute for bulk degreasing
strike or plating current decisions downstream

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a supplier sheet sanctioning a different polarity regime for a substrate this shop runs, or failure clustering that implicates the current polarity map

pros.claim: Choosing polarity by mechanism prevents the two classic invisible failures at once - smut plate-out and hydrogen charging
pros.example: a steel clasp run anodic comes out gate-clean, where the same clasp run cathodic passes visually but carries a smut film that peels the nickel strike a day later

cons.claim: The polarity logic differs by substrate, so a mixed bench day invites setup errors
cons.example: after a morning of steel run anodic, a brass locket left at the same setting too long comes out with its color-buffed face visibly dulled

failure_modes: reversed leads because plating habit says work-is-cathode
electrocleaning over remaining bulk soil and burning it on
extended anodic time tarnishing copper alloys
high-foam cleaner in an electro cell trapping evolved gas mixtures at the surface
acceptance_tests: the lead polarity is checked against the substrate class on the docket before current is applied, and the following water-break gate passes
revisit_triggers: gate failures that cluster after the electroclean stage rather than the soak
a substrate class new to the line needing a polarity ruling from its supplier sheet

nodes.definition: Operate the water-break test as the binary gate between cleaning and everything after it: withdraw the racked work from clean rinse water and watch the film - on a chemically clean surface water sheets unbroken over every face and edge (shop practice watches it hold for roughly half a minute), while any beading, pulling back, or dry island announces remaining organics and fails the piece. The test costs nothing, takes seconds, and is the only instant cleanliness verdict the bench has, which is why the rule attached to it is absolute: failing work goes backward to degrease, never forward with a plan to make it up later. The one way the gate lies is surfactant masking - drag-out of a heavily wetted cleaner can sheet over a still-soiled surface - so the reading is taken after honest rinsing, and a suspicious pass on a piece from a fresh, surfactant-rich cleaner is re-rinsed warm and read again.

included: running and reading the test on racked jewelry
excluded: adhesion testing of finished plate (QC territory)
judging oxide or passivity, which the gate cannot see

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an interface failure analysis contradicting a recorded gate pass, or adoption of an instrumented cleanliness check that changes the gate's role

pros.claim: A free, instant, binary gate placed mid-chain converts invisible contamination into a visible stop signal
pros.example: a pendant that looks mirror-clean shows a beading crescent at its bail where compound hid, and the loop back to soak costs minutes instead of a strip-and-replate

cons.claim: The gate only sees organics, so a clean pass says nothing about oxide or passivity
cons.example: a stainless piece can sheet perfectly and still refuse to bond because its chromium oxide film is untouched by everything the gate measures

failure_modes: reading the test through surfactant drag-out and passing a soiled piece
waving a marginal read through under schedule pressure
testing one face of the piece and missing beading in recessed geometry
acceptance_tests: the pass is recorded per load with the operator's read, and any fail can be shown to have looped the work back to degrease rather than forward
revisit_triggers: a piece that passed the gate later fails adhesion with an organic signature at the interface
a cleaner change that alters wetting behavior enough to change how reads look

nodes.definition: Translate the docket's verified substrate class into the correct activation path, because activation is where the chain forks and a wrong fork is destructive. The working map a jewelry bench needs: brass, copper, and jeweler's bronze take a mild acid dip to cut tarnish and flash oxide, with pickle severity deliberately skipped; sterling and silver-plated work takes gentle activation that respects a surface already free of scale; mild steel takes a true pickle for oxide before its activation dip; zinc die-cast diverts to the minimal-chemistry caution path; stainless and aged or previously plated nickel divert to the passive-substrate handoff because no dip alone defeats a self-healing film. Every branch is a commercial product run per its TDS - what this node owns is choosing the branch from the verified class, never from appearance, and refusing to activate anything whose class the docket leaves ambiguous.

excluded: pickle mechanics and passive-film handling detail (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new accepted substrate class, a supplier activation product change, or a wrong-branch failure that shows the map's classes are drawn too coarsely

pros.claim: A written branch map turns the most consequential chemistry decision on the line into a lookup instead of a judgment call
pros.example: a white-metal charm the docket calls zinc die-cast routes to the mild path automatically, where an appearance-based guess of silver would have sent it into acid that eats pot metal

cons.claim: A map keyed to classes fails on genuinely mixed construction
cons.example: a brass box chain with steel jump rings and a soldered white-metal clasp spans three branches at once, and the map alone cannot say which chemistry the assembly as a whole survives

failure_modes: activating by appearance when the docket is missing or vague
running a mixed-metal assembly down a single-branch path
applying steel-severity acid to copper alloys because the tank was already set up
acceptance_tests: for each substrate class the shop accepts, the map names one activation branch, its commercial product, and the classes explicitly excluded from that branch
an ambiguous-class test docket is refused back to assessment rather than activated
revisit_triggers: a new substrate class or plated-over construction enters the shop's accepted work
an adhesion failure that traces to a wrong-branch activation

nodes.definition: Run the acid pickle as the oxide-class removal step on substrates that need it, chiefly mild steel findings and heat-scaled or heavily tarnished work: the acid dissolves oxide down to bare metal, and the operating rule is the shortest exposure that yields a uniformly active surface, because everything past that point is damage - over-pickling pits the base metal, charges steel with hydrogen, and on high-carbon parts raises a black smut that itself must then be removed. Inhibited pickle products exist precisely to protect the base metal once oxide is gone and are chosen per TDS. The tank ages by iron loading: published handbook practice treats a rising dissolved-iron load and visibly slowed pickling as the dump signal class, with the exact criterion taken from the product sheet. Pickle tanks are non-metallic, lidded when idle because acid fumes corrode every tool in the room, and their fume path and drains obey the segregation and layout rules.

included: oxide and scale dissolution on substrates the map sends here
excluded: zinc die-cast and copper-alloy work (their branches forbid this severity)
waste disposal mechanics beyond naming the obligation class

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a pickle product change, logged exposure drift, or a substrate mix shift that changes how much scaled steel work the line actually sees

pros.claim: A correct pickle is the only way a scaled or rusted steel surface becomes platable at all
pros.example: a batch of blued-steel clasp springs comes out of a short inhibited pickle uniformly matte gray and takes its strike, where no amount of degreasing would have touched the oxide

cons.claim: The pickle is the most destructive tank on the line when held too long
cons.example: a delicate steel finding left in through a phone call comes out pitted and undersized, and no later plating step can rebuild the detail

failure_modes: over-pickling into pitting and hydrogen charging
pickling over residual organics and pitting under the soil
running the tank far past its iron-loading life because it still bubbles
leaving the tank unlidded and rusting every steel tool on the bench
acceptance_tests: pickled work shows a uniform matte active surface with detail edges intact, and the exposure used is logged as the shortest that achieved it
revisit_triggers: pickling time drifting upward against the log, indicating iron loading
pitting or smut appearing at exposures that previously ran clean

nodes.definition: Keep the final dilute acid dip in its precise role: a seconds-long immersion immediately before transfer that resets the flash oxide a cleaned surface grows during rinsing and air exposure, so bare active metal - not a minutes-old oxide film - meets the first deposit. The dip does not clean, does not pickle, and cannot rescue a failed gate; its entire value is in when it happens, which is why it lives at the end of the line physically adjacent to the tank it feeds. Because it is small, cheap, and mildly acidic, it doubles as a sacrificial contamination buffer protecting the tank after it, and the corresponding discipline is dumping it on a short cycle per its TDS rather than letting it become a contamination reservoir. The dip's clock-starting property is the handover into transfer discipline: from the moment the piece leaves this dip, its activation is decaying.

included: sacrificial-buffer role and short dump cycle

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a line re-layout changing the dip-to-tank distance, or failure evidence that the current dump cycle lets the dip itself contaminate work

pros.claim: A seconds-long dip at the right moment buys more adhesion than minutes of extra cleaning at the wrong one
pros.example: steel findings that sat in rinse water while a rack was rebuilt re-enter through the dip and strike cleanly, where the same findings transferred directly would carry a fresh oxide film into the tank

cons.claim: Because the dip looks trivial it gets treated as optional or as a parking spot
cons.example: an operator holds pieces in the dip while answering the counter, and the extended acid exposure etches the color-buffed brass surface the dip was only meant to kiss

failure_modes: skipping the dip because the piece was pickled minutes ago
using the dip as a holding bath
running the dip long past its dump cycle until it deposits the contamination it was meant to absorb
acceptance_tests: the dip is the last chemistry before transfer on every activated load, and its dump log shows the short cycle its sheet prescribes
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures on work that passed all gates but sat between rinse and tank without a final dip

nodes.definition: Own the prep line's answer to substrates whose oxide heals itself: stainless steel re-grows its chromium oxide film within seconds of any strip, and aged or previously plated nickel passivates similarly, so no soak, gate pass, pickle, or dip - however perfect - produces a surface that stays bondable long enough to transfer. The only mechanism that works is simultaneous strip-and-deposit: a live-entry strike (Wood's-nickel class) where current is flowing before the work enters, holding the surface depassivated in the same instant a thin bonded layer covers it. Operating that strike bath is the downstream plating bench's work; what this node owns is the boundary duties - recognizing from the docket which work is passive-class, refusing to treat it with ordinary activation, scheduling the piece so it arrives at the strike station without a waiting period, and flagging the no-rinse-delay rule between strike and next plate so the strike's fresh surface is not passivated by the prep line's own rinse discipline.

included: recognizing passive-class work from the docket
why dips cannot defeat self-healing films
scheduling and flag duties into the strike handoff
excluded: strike bath make-up, current settings, and operation (plating bench, per its TDS)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: failure evidence widening or narrowing the passive class this shop actually meets, or a strike-station process change that alters the handoff timing rules

pros.claim: Naming passivity as its own class stops the bench from burning hours repeating ever-harsher cleaning on a surface that was never dirty
pros.example: a stainless watch bracelet that keeps shedding its gold gets routed to the live-entry strike after one docket check, instead of a third trip through soak, electroclean, and a stronger dip

cons.claim: The handoff splits responsibility across two benches, and the seam is where pieces stall
cons.example: prep finishes a stainless lot at closing time, the strike station is cold, and by morning the lot is passive again with nothing visible to show it

failure_modes: treating stainless like mild steel because both say steel on the docket
a long rinse or wait after strike quietly re-passivating the fresh surface
assuming old nickel plate under a refinish job is still active because it was once plated
acceptance_tests: every passive-class docket routes to the strike handoff with a scheduled, waiting-free arrival, and no passive-class piece is logged through ordinary activation
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures on refinish work over old nickel, indicating the passive class is broader than the current docket flags
a strike-station schedule change that lengthens the handoff wait

nodes.definition: Protect the substrate class that prep chemistry destroys fastest: zinc die-cast (pot metal) costume pieces are reactive, porous, and often the customer's sentimental item, and ordinary acids attack them within seconds - frothing, pitting, and dissolving detail that no one can restore. The caution path is minimal chemistry throughout: mild cleaner exposure, the gentlest sanctioned activation, short cycles, and fast transfers, all per products whose TDS covers zinc die-cast. Porosity adds a second trap: the casting soaks up solution and weeps it back out later, so trapped chemistry causes spotting and blistering after plating even when every visible step went well - which argues for restrained immersion times and generous drain and rinse dwell. The judgment this node forces is honest triage feedback: when a die-cast piece cannot be made clean within its chemistry tolerance, the answer is back to assessment for a refuse-or-refer decision, never a stronger acid to keep the job.

included: minimal-chemistry cycle design for zinc die-cast
return-to-triage when tolerance and cleanliness conflict

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an incident on a die-cast customer piece, or supplier products extending or shrinking what chemistry the class tolerates

pros.claim: A named caution path converts the line's most frequent customer-piece disaster into a routed, restrained procedure
pros.example: a 1950s pot-metal brooch runs mild cleaner, seconds of sanctioned activation, and fast transfer, and comes out platable, where the standard brass path would have frothed its hinge detail away

cons.claim: Minimal chemistry sometimes cannot reach cleanliness at all, and the path has no stronger tool to offer
cons.example: decades of embedded polish and corrosion in a porous casting keep failing the gate at exposures the substrate tolerates, and the only honest outputs are refusal or referral

failure_modes: one dip in a standard acid tank destroying detail in seconds
porosity weeping trapped solution into later spotting and blistering
repeating mild cycles far past the point where return-to-triage was the correct call
acceptance_tests: die-cast work can be shown to have touched only branch-sanctioned products at logged short exposures, and any piece that could not reach the gate within tolerance is documented back to assessment
revisit_triggers: post-plate spotting or blistering on die-cast jobs indicating trapped solution
a die-cast-compatible product change on the line

nodes.definition: Design the rinse system as staged counterflow rather than one big rinse: the piece moves through two or three rinse tanks toward ever-cleaner water while fresh make-up enters at the clean end and overflows toward the dirty end, so each stage dilutes what the previous one left. Standard rinse-ratio math is the reason this is not optional on a small bench - a cascade achieves with modest water what a single overflowing tank cannot achieve at any affordable flow. Two placements are load-bearing: a rinse after every chemistry so no tank's solution rides into the next, and a dead (static) rinse ahead of critical tanks, which soaks up drag-in as a sacrificial buffer and, placed before gold, captures dragged-out metal value for recovery instead of the drain. The design work is deciding stage counts, flow direction, and which tanks earn a dead rinse, with the conductivity pen as the instrument that later tells whether the design is working.

included: counterflow staging, stage counts, and flow direction
excluded: water purity grades per stage (its own node)
the contamination routes themselves (drag control node)
effluent treatment beyond naming the obligation class

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a line re-layout, water cost or supply change, or logged rinse readings showing a stage count that is too low or wastefully high

pros.claim: Cascade staging cuts water use by orders of magnitude while rinsing better than any single tank
pros.example: three cascaded tubs after the pickle keep the final rinse reading near its make-up water on the pen, at a small fraction of the flow one always-running rinse would demand

cons.claim: More stages mean more vessels, more bench space, and more tanks to maintain and log
cons.example: a cramped studio that squeezes in a five-stage line finds two of the stages never get dumped on schedule, and the neglected stages become the contamination source the design was meant to prevent

failure_modes: one shared rinse serving multiple chemistries and bridging them
flow plumbed the wrong way so make-up water enters at the dirty end
no dead rinse before the gold tank, sending metal value down the drain with every load
acceptance_tests: the line diagram shows a rinse after every chemistry, counterflow direction marked, and a dead rinse ahead of each critical tank
revisit_triggers: conductivity at any final stage creeping toward its dirty end despite normal flow
a new tank or chemistry added to the line

nodes.definition: Assign the right water to each rinse duty and give the bench an instrument to police it: early rinse stages after cleaners and pickles can run on tap water, but final rinses before critical tanks and all bath make-up run on deionized or reverse-osmosis water, because tap chloride and hardness minerals are named contaminants of nickel and gold chemistries and a final rinse is only as clean as the water it is made of. The control instrument is the conductivity (TDS) pen: cheap, instant, and sufficient to gate a final rinse against its setpoint - a handbook-class practice puts final-rinse conductivity before critical tanks in the low tens of microsiemens range, referenced here strictly as a handbook-class band with the shop's own setpoint written in its log. Water quality also decays invisibly - DI cartridges exhaust without ceremony - so the pen readings are taken on a cadence, not on suspicion.

excluded: asserting a universal numeric conductivity threshold as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a water-supply change, DI equipment change, or downstream bath contamination traced to rinse water grade

pros.claim: Grading water by duty spends purity only where it protects chemistry, keeping DI consumption affordable
pros.example: tap water carries the heavy dilution work after the soak while a few liters of DI hold the final rinse at its setpoint, instead of running the whole line on cartridge water

cons.claim: A two-grade system invites grade mix-ups that are invisible to the eye
cons.example: a helper tops up the final rinse from the tap kettle, the pen would have caught it instantly, but nobody reads the pen until spotting shows up on the next plated batch

failure_modes: final rinse quietly running on tap water
an exhausted DI cartridge feeding water that reads like tap
no logged setpoint, so readings exist but gate nothing
acceptance_tests: each rinse stage has a written water grade and the final stages have a logged conductivity setpoint with dated pen readings against it
revisit_triggers: pen readings drifting upward at constant duty, indicating cartridge exhaustion or upstream drag-in growth

nodes.definition: Control the specific routes by which one tank poisons the next, because on a prep line contamination almost never walks in the door - it rides the work. The named routes a jewelry bench must know: alkaline cleaner dragged into the pickle neutralizes it and, if silicated, gels on the work; acid dragged into an alkaline tank wastes both; and the money route, cleaner surfactants, chloride, and nickel ions dragged toward the gold tank, are listed poisons of gold chemistry that show up as bath performance decay long after the causal load. Countermeasures are unglamorous and effective: deliberate drain dwell over each tank before moving on, rinses honestly worked between chemistries, hollow and cupped geometry tipped to empty, racks rinsed as carefully as work, and the dead rinse absorbing what remains. Drag control is also the diagnostic lens: when a downstream bath sickens, the first question is which upstream tank changed, not what is wrong with the bath.

included: named drag-in routes and their countermeasures
drain dwell and rack rinsing practice
drag-in as the first suspect for downstream bath decay

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: downstream bath analysis implicating a drag route not on the current list, or geometry classes that defeat the current drain practices

pros.claim: Naming the routes turns contamination from bad luck into a checklist the bench can actually run
pros.example: when the pickle starts gelling, the bench checks silicate carry-over and rinse dwell after the soak instead of dumping acid twice a week and wondering

cons.claim: Full drag discipline slows every transfer, and the cost is paid on every load while the benefit shows only statistically
cons.example: ten extra seconds of drain dwell per tank per load feels like nothing until a forty-piece day, when the temptation to hurry returns exactly as the gold tank is most exposed

failure_modes: hollow geometry carrying a hidden reservoir of cleaner through every later tank
racks never rinsed, re-contaminating each load they carry
diagnosing a sick gold bath as a bath problem while the upstream drag route stays open
acceptance_tests: each chemistry-to-chemistry transfer on the line has a stated drain-and-rinse practice, and cupped geometry has a tipping orientation noted at racking
revisit_triggers: any downstream bath decay, which fires this node before bath chemistry is touched
a new piece geometry class (deep hollows, tubes) entering the shop's work

nodes.definition: Enforce the handling rule that protects everything the chain has bought: from the water-break pass to tank entry, the piece is touched only by its rack, wires, hooks, or clean dedicated tools - never by fingers, and never by shop gloves that have handled compound, money, or lunch. A single fingerprint redeposits exactly the organic film the whole chain just removed, and the failure is invisible: the print will not show until it ghosts through the gold as a stain or a peel. The rule's teeth are its recovery cost: a touched piece goes back to soak and starts the chain again, because a wipe with a cloth is itself a re-soiling event, not a fix. Supporting practice lives here too - clean tool stations at every point a piece might need repositioning, rack designs that let every later operation happen without re-gripping, and the bench habit of narrating touches so an accidental one is confessed and looped back instead of hidden.

included: the rack-and-tool-only rule after the gate
excluded: handling before the gate (ordinary shop care)
glove and PPE selection for chemical protection (safety territory)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fingerprint-signature defects on plated work, or a rack redesign that changes where repositioning is needed

pros.claim: A bright-line rule with a known recovery price is followed more honestly than a be-careful admonition
pros.example: an operator who steadies a swinging pendant with a thumb says so and re-runs it from soak, because the rule made the cost explicit instead of arguable

cons.claim: No-touch handling makes some jewelry operations genuinely awkward and slower
cons.example: re-hanging a slipped chain onto its hook using only tools takes three times as long as fingers would, and on a bad rack design it risks dropping the piece instead

failure_modes: the reflexive steadying touch nobody reports
clean-looking gloves that carry compound from the finishing bench
wiping a touched piece with a cloth and calling it recovered
acceptance_tests: post-gate handling on the line is observably rack-and-tool-only, and any logged touch event shows a restart at soak rather than a wipe
revisit_triggers: stains or peel patterns on plated work consistent with fingerprint geometry

nodes.definition: Rack or wire the work once, correctly, before the first tank, because racking decisions echo through every later step: the contact must be electrically firm for the electroclean and downstream plating stations (a loose contact reads later as stepped or burned deposits), the contact point is placed on the least visible surface because it will shadow chemistry and current alike and leave its small mark, and orientation is chosen so cupped and hollow geometry drains rather than carrying solution tank to tank and so evolved gas can escape instead of pocketing against a face. Jewelry racking is its own small craft - copper or titanium wire hooks, plastisol-coated rack fingers, loops that hold a ring without scoring its band - and the governing rule is that a piece racked so it must be re-gripped mid-chain is a piece racked wrong, since every re-grip is a handling event and, after the gate, a restart.

excluded: rack materials engineering beyond bench practice
current distribution design in plating tanks (downstream)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: contact-mark complaints, deposit defects traced to racking, or new piece geometries entering the shop's accepted work

pros.claim: One correct racking amortizes across every station and eliminates mid-chain handling entirely
pros.example: a bracelet wired with two hidden clasp-side contacts and a drain-down orientation runs soak to tank entry without a single re-grip

cons.claim: Contact points are unavoidable small sacrifices and choosing them needs the customer's eye in mind
cons.example: a contact placed on the presentation face of a locket leaves its ghost exactly where the owner looks, converting good plating into a complaint

failure_modes: loose contact discovered only as a burned deposit downstream
cupped geometry racked mouth-up, ladling solution into every tank
racking that requires a mid-chain re-grip and forces a restart
acceptance_tests: each racked load shows firm contact at a hidden point and a drain-and-vent orientation, verified before the first immersion
revisit_triggers: burned or stepped deposits traced to contact quality, or a new geometry class the current rack stock cannot hold correctly

nodes.definition: Run the interval between activation and tank entry as a clocked, wet, short transfer, because an activated surface is a decaying asset: activated steel blooms visible flash rust within around a minute in air, copper alloys re-grow flash oxide invisibly on a similar timescale, and struck passive substrates re-passivate in a rinse delay - handbook-class practice puts acceptable transfer windows in the well-under-a-minute class, cited here as a class while the shop times its own line. The rules that follow: the piece travels wet, never dried and never allowed to dry; the physical path from final dip to tank is arranged in steps, not strides; and when the clock is blown - a phone call, a dropped rack, a visible orange bloom - the only correct recovery is back through activation, never proceeding on the theory that it was only a minute. The clock also disciplines batch size: no more work is activated at once than the bench can transfer inside the window.

excluded: in-tank entry technique (live entry belongs to the plating bench)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the shop's own timed-path measurements, end-of-batch failure clustering, or a re-layout changing transfer distances

pros.claim: Treating transfer as a clocked step makes an invisible decay visible and manageable
pros.example: the bench activates six pieces, not sixteen, because six is what reaches the tank inside the window - and the adhesion complaint rate on steel work drops accordingly

cons.claim: Clock discipline collides with how a small shop actually runs - interruptions are constant
cons.example: the counter bell rings mid-transfer, and the honest cost of answering it is a re-activation loop the operator must choose to pay

failure_modes: work drying between dip and tank
plating over an invisible flash oxide because no bloom showed
batch sizes that guarantee the last pieces blow the window every time
proceeding after a delay because the surface still looks bright
acceptance_tests: the shop has timed its own dip-to-tank path per station, batch sizes are set from that timing, and any logged delay event shows a re-activation rather than a proceed
revisit_triggers: flash rust or adhesion failures clustering on end-of-batch pieces
a layout change altering the walk between dip and tank

nodes.definition: Lay the physical line out so the correct process is the easy one and the fatal one is impossible: tanks in run order left to right so the chain's sequence is walked, not remembered; the final dip adjacent to the tank it feeds so the transfer clock is winnable; rinses between chemistries where the hand naturally goes; acid stations and any cyanide-bearing products in separated zones with separate drains, spill paths, and storage per the segregation rules; fume extraction over acid and electroclean positions with lids on idle tanks; secondary containment under everything; and labels on every vessel including rinse tubs, because an unlabeled tub is where segregation quietly dies. Layout is also where jurisdictional obligations become physical - eyewash reach, ventilation, storage separation - so a layout review is the natural moment for the verify-your-local-rules check. The node's test of success is that a stranger who knows the chain could run the line correctly from its geography alone.

included: segregated zones, drains, containment, labels, extraction
layout review as the jurisdiction-check moment
excluded: the segregation doctrine itself (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a bench move, new equipment, a spill or near-miss, or updated local workplace rules changing what the geography must provide

pros.claim: Geography enforces procedure with zero ongoing willpower
pros.example: because the only path from pickle to tank passes the rinse and the dip in order, the hurried version of the job and the correct version are the same walk

cons.claim: A bench-scale room rarely permits the ideal geography, forcing documented compromises
cons.example: when the sole floor drain sits in the acid zone, the alkaline and any cyanide-free-substituted products need pumped or carried waste paths, which must be written down or they will be improvised badly

failure_modes: a layout that forces backtracking past open tanks with wet work
unlabeled rinse tubs migrating between zones
the dip landing far from the tank it feeds, making every transfer a sprint
no secondary containment under a tank that eventually leaks
acceptance_tests: a line walk confirms run-order geography, dip-to-tank adjacency, separated zones and drains, labeled vessels, containment, and extraction over the positions that need it
revisit_triggers: any new tank, product, or bench move
a near-miss or spill event anywhere on the line

nodes.definition: Track every prep solution's working life and dump it on evidence, not on smell or calendar alone: cleaners are titrated or control-tested per their TDS, and the great bench-visible signal is performance drift - when normal soil takes twice the normal time, the tank is telling you it is done regardless of how it looks; pickles age by iron loading and slowing action; the activation dip turns over on a short cycle by design; and every tank's load count and additions live in the bench log so drift is a measured line, not a feeling. The economics justify the discipline: prep chemicals are among the cheapest consumables in the shop while every failure they cause is paid in stripped and replated gold, so stretching a tired cleaner is the worst trade available. Spent solutions are named waste classes - spent pickle liquor, alkaline cleaner concentrate - handled per the shop's jurisdiction-verified disposal obligations, never down an unexamined drain.

included: TDS-anchored life tracking and control tests
load logging and spent-solution obligation classes
excluded: waste treatment mechanics and jurisdictional numeric limits
gold and underplate bath maintenance (downstream benches)
improvised regeneration a TDS does not sanction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: control-test results diverging from the log's predictions, a product change, or a volume change that shifts which aging mode dominates

pros.claim: Logged life tracking catches exhaustion before the gate does, which is a full batch earlier
pros.example: the log shows soak times creeping across two weeks, so the cleaner is remade on a quiet morning instead of failing a customer batch on a busy one

cons.claim: On a low-volume bench, calendar aging and load aging diverge, and the sheet's assumptions may fit neither
cons.example: a cleaner that sees three loads a week may die of carbonation and evaporation long before its rated load count, which only the control test - not the counter - will show

failure_modes: running a cleaner until the water-break gate fails a batch
topping up a pickle indefinitely instead of dumping at its iron-loading signal
no log, so every judgment starts from zero information
pouring a spent solution into an unexamined drain
acceptance_tests: each tank has a log of make-up date, loads, additions, and control-test results, and the last dump of each tank can be tied to a recorded signal rather than a guess
revisit_triggers: gate failure rates rising while all tanks are nominally in life
a product change resetting what the control tests and life signals are

nodes.definition: Read adhesion failures backward into the chain, because each failure signature names its own suspect: whole-stack blistering or sheet peel points to soil or oxide under the first deposit - a failed or lied-to water-break gate, a dry-out between tanks, or a dead surface at entry; peel that appears only over old plate points to a passive interface the handoff should have caught; a dark, spongy, zero-adhesion deposit is the classic immersion-deposit signature of unstruck metal meeting an acid bath; paint-like peeling with a hazy film underneath is silicate carry-over; fingerprint-shaped stains or peels are a handling event; and spotting or blister-weep on die-cast is trapped solution talking. The discipline is running this ladder before touching any bath chemistry - most plating failures are prep failures, and the bath is the last suspect, not the first. Each diagnosis feeds a correction to the implicated node and, on customer work, an honest account of what happened.

included: feeding corrections back to the implicated node
excluded: QC acceptance testing of good work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an unclassifiable failure signature, or a failure whose confirmed root cause contradicts the ladder's mapping

pros.claim: A signature ladder finds root cause in minutes and protects healthy baths from ritual dumping
pros.example: a sheet-peel on a steel clasp sends the bench to the gate log and the transfer clock, and the actual fault - a blown transfer during a busy hour - surfaces without a liter of chemistry being wasted

cons.claim: Signatures overlap, and a single failed piece may genuinely underdetermine its cause
cons.example: peel at one edge could be a handling touch, a rack shadow, or a marginal gate read, and only the next controlled piece through the chain distinguishes them

failure_modes: dumping the gold bath first on every failure
reworking the failed piece without diagnosing, guaranteeing a repeat
not recording failures, so patterns across weeks stay invisible
acceptance_tests: each logged failure carries a signature classification, the implicated prep node, and the correction applied before the next comparable piece ran
revisit_triggers: a failure signature the current ladder cannot classify
repeat failures at one node despite applied corrections, meaning the diagnosis - not just the step - is wrong

nodes.definition: Define plate-ready operationally and release nothing without it: a piece leaves the prep line for a tank only when the water-break pass is on record for this cleaning cycle, the activation branch actually run matches the docket's substrate class, the transfer clock is live - the piece is wet and inside its window or being handed into a live-entry strike without delay - the no-touch chain is unbroken since the gate, and the final rinse it passed met its logged conductivity setpoint. The release record is one line in the bench log tying piece, docket, gate result, branch, and clock together; it costs seconds and is the artifact the downstream bench, the failure diagnosis, and the customer conversation all lean on later. The release rule has no rush-job exemption, because the release moment is precisely where schedule pressure historically converts into strip-and-replate: an unreleased piece waits as work in progress, and a piece that cannot meet a condition loops back to the node that owns it.

included: the five release conditions and their evidence
excluded: in-tank quality from this point on (plating benches)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a failure on released work or a downstream rejection, either of which forces re-examining the five conditions and their evidence

pros.claim: A recorded definition of done turns prep from a vibe into a contract the downstream bench can trust
pros.example: the plating bench takes a released rack without re-inspecting it, because the release line shows gate, branch, and clock, and the last hundred releases have held up

cons.claim: A release gate adds a formal step to every single load on a bench that may be one person deep
cons.example: on a twenty-load day the operator writes twenty release lines, and the temptation to batch them at day's end - destroying their evidentiary value - is real

failure_modes: releasing on memory of a gate pass from the previous cycle
a rush job released with a blown clock because the tank was ready
release lines written after the fact from reconstruction
acceptance_tests: every tank entry on the line can be matched to a contemporaneous release line carrying all five conditions, and sampled releases withstand comparison against the gate and clock logs they cite
revisit_triggers: any adhesion failure on released work, which audits the release conditions themselves
a downstream bench reporting released work that arrived not ready

edges.why_related: the soak is the organic rung of the soil-class ladder the mission defines, and its position first in the chain comes from that ladder
rinse staging exists to keep each rung of the ladder from poisoning the next, so its design is derived from the chain's sequence
racking choices (contact placement, orientation) are made against the docket's substrate class and flags, so the docket must be in hand first
the activation map is keyed by the docket's verified substrate class; without the docket there is no legitimate key
soak concentration, temperature, and control tests are transcribed from the cleaner's TDS, which the discipline puts on file
the electrocleaner's window and any sanctioned cathodic or periodic-reverse regime come from its sheet; the polarity map defers to it
life tracking runs on the control tests and dump criteria each product's sheet defines
the layout exists partly to make segregation physical - zones, drains, storage - so the doctrine precedes the geography
only gate-passed work may be activated; activating a soiled surface locks contamination under the deposit
the pickle serves only the substrate classes the map routes to it; severity unkeyed to class is how pieces are destroyed
the final dip's chemistry class is chosen per the map's branch for the substrate in hand
the map's stainless and old-nickel branches terminate in the handoff rather than in any dip
the die-cast caution path is the map's minimal-chemistry branch, entered only by verified class
the clock starts when the piece leaves the dip; the transfer rules have no start point without it
passive-class work gives the clock its tightest case - repassivation in a rinse delay - so the handoff defines part of what the clock must beat
water grades are assigned per stage, and the stages exist only once the cascade is designed
drag countermeasures assume the rinse-between-every-chemistry structure the design provides
the no-touch rule's start line is the gate pass; before it, handling is ordinary shop care
an unbroken no-touch chain since the gate is one of the five release conditions
a live clock at the moment of entry is a release condition; a blown clock loops the piece back instead
a recorded gate pass for the current cleaning cycle is the first release condition
no-touch handling is only achievable when the racking already supports every later operation without a re-grip
the soak takes the bulk load first so cavitation energy is spent on recesses, not on gross soil the cheap tank handles
the gate reads the surface immediately after the last cleaning step, so the electroclean's output is exactly what the test judges
on the steel branch the pickle precedes the final dip, which resets the flash oxide the post-pickle rinse grows
the pickle is an acid station, so its placement, drains, rinse vessels, and waste path are bound by the segregation doctrine wherever any cyanide-bearing product exists on site
the first immersion is where the entry rule bites: no docket, no soak, whatever the schedule says
pickle strength, inhibitor use, and dump criteria are bounded by the product sheet; no improvised acid blend is run
release requires the final rinse to have met its logged conductivity setpoint; water grade failures block release
uncontrolled drag-in is a dominant driver of solution aging - it neutralizes, loads, and contaminates tanks ahead of their natural life
blown transfer windows are a leading generator of the whole-stack peel signatures the diagnosis ladder classifies
an exhausted cleaner surfaces as rising gate failure rates - the gate is where dead tanks are finally seen
organic-signature failures loop corrections into the degreasing stations - product, temperature, time, or dump cadence
wrong-branch and passive-interface failures redraw the map's classes or flags rather than just reworking the piece
gate failures clustering after a passing soak point the review at electroclean polarity, settings, or solution condition
the pickle's job is aggressive oxide removal and the die-cast path's job is keeping acid off a substrate acids destroy; a die-cast piece with real corrosion sits exactly between them
edges.resolution_rule: substrate survival wins absolutely: die-cast work never enters pickle-severity acid, and if the caution path's mild chemistry cannot reach the gate, the piece goes back to assessment for refuse-or-refer rather than up the severity ladder

edges.why_related: cavitation wants to reach every recess, and the intake gate exists to keep vulnerable construction - which cavitation can break - off the line; hollow or repaired pieces the docket under-flags sit in the gap
edges.resolution_rule: the gate wins: any construction doubt discovered at the ultrasonic stops the cycle and returns the piece to assessment with the observation, and the docket fields are amended so the class is flagged next time; the cycle is never finished first to save the cleaning

edges.why_related: the design node optimizes for water thrift and few vessels while the quality node demands purity where it matters; a stage cut to save water can be the stage that let conductivity through
edges.resolution_rule: purity wins at the critical end and thrift wins early: the final-rinse conductivity setpoint is never sacrificed to stage-count economy, and any water saving is taken in the early tap-grade stages where dilution, not purity, is the job

edges.why_related: when the window is nearly spent the operator is tempted to skip the re-dip and sprint for the tank, trading the dip's oxide reset against the clock's remaining seconds
edges.resolution_rule: the dip wins and the clock restarts: a piece near or past its window goes back through activation, because seconds of re-dip are recoverable while an oxide film under gold is a strip-and-replate; the schedule absorbs the loop, the interface does not

conflict_axes.name: throughput_versus_gate_integrity
conflict_axes.description: Every gate on the line - water-break, release, the fail-backward loops - costs time on every load, and schedule pressure argues for waving marginal work through; the entire value of a gate is that it never negotiates.
poles: move the batch, judge marginal reads generously
hold every gate binary, loop failures backward
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gates never flex; capacity does - shrink batch sizes and adjust promises to customers rather than adjusting what counts as a pass

conflict_axes.name: cleaning_aggression_versus_substrate_survival
conflict_axes.description: Hotter, stronger, longer cleaning removes soil faster but the same aggression pits zinc die-cast, opens solder seams, dulls color-buffed alloys, and etches detail that cannot be restored.
poles: escalate chemistry until the soil is gone
cap chemistry at what the substrate tolerates
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the substrate class sets a hard ceiling per the activation map; work that cannot reach cleanliness under its ceiling returns to assessment rather than exceeding it

conflict_axes.name: anodic_scrub_versus_surface_preservation
conflict_axes.description: Anodic electrocleaning is the mechanistically safe polarity for steel but its mild surface dissolution and oxidation dulls tarnish-prone copper alloys; cathodic coverage is gentler on the finish but plates smut and charges hydrogen.
poles: anodic scrubbing for interface integrity
gentler regimes to protect the delivered finish
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: polarity follows the substrate class and the supplier sheet: anodic on steel, time-limited anodic or a sheet-sanctioned regime on copper alloys, never habit from the previous load

conflict_axes.name: water_thrift_versus_rinse_purity
conflict_axes.description: Water and DI cartridges cost money and bench space, and cascade staging exists to save them - but the final rinse before a critical tank has a purity job that no thrift argument may touch.
poles: minimize water, stages, and DI consumption
guarantee final-rinse purity at its setpoint
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split the line: thrift governs the early tap-grade dilution stages, purity governs the final stages, and the conductivity setpoint is the boundary marker between the regimes

conflict_axes.name: bath_life_economy_versus_dump_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Prep solutions cost little but remaking them costs an hour, so tanks get stretched - while every batch run through a dying cleaner gambles gold-value rework against cleaner-value savings.
poles: stretch solution life to the last load
dump on the first credible exhaustion signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: price the trade honestly: the downside of a dump is one quiet hour, the downside of a stretch is stripped and replated gold plus a customer conversation - so the exhaustion signal wins

conflict_axes.name: transfer_speed_versus_handling_care
conflict_axes.description: The clock says sprint from dip to tank; the no-touch and racking rules say a controlled, tool-only movement - and a rushed transfer is exactly when a piece gets steadied with a thumb or dropped.
poles: beat the clock at any handling cost
move deliberately with rack and tools only
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: solve it with geography and batch size, not heroics: a dip adjacent to its tank and fewer pieces per batch make the careful transfer and the fast transfer the same transfer

conflict_axes.name: one_bench_versatility_versus_segregation
conflict_axes.description: A small shop wants one flexible bench where every tank is reachable; segregation doctrine wants zones, separate drains, and distance between chemistries that must never meet.
poles: compact multi-use bench, everything at arm's reach
zoned layout with hard separation and duplicate vessels
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: segregation is non-negotiable where cyanide exists at all; the versatile-bench desire is satisfied legitimately by choosing cyanide-free products and deleting the hazard class, never by shrinking the separation

conflict_axes.name: customer_piece_caution_versus_job_completion
conflict_axes.description: The shop is paid for finished jobs, and sending work back to assessment - or refusing it - costs revenue and goodwill now, while a destroyed sentimental piece costs far more later and cannot be bought back.
poles: find a way to run the piece and finish the job
loop doubtful pieces back to triage regardless of the schedule
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: irreversibility decides: where the downside is a destroyed customer piece, the caution pole wins without a balancing test, and the revenue conversation moves to expectation-setting at intake

conflict_axes.name: cavitation_reach_versus_construction_risk
conflict_axes.description: The ultrasonic is the only tool that degreases deep recesses, and the same energy opens weak solder seams and lifting films - the recess-heavy pieces that most need it are often the fragile ones.
poles: full ultrasonic coverage for guaranteed recess cleanliness
restrict cavitation exposure on doubtful construction
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: doubt routes backward, not onward: construction questions belong to assessment, and the ultrasonic operator's discovery of one is a docket amendment, never a judgment call to finish the cycle

conflict_axes.name: prep_scrutiny_versus_bath_blame
conflict_axes.description: When plated work fails, dumping a bath feels decisive and inspecting one's own prep feels accusatory - so healthy chemistry gets replaced while the actual prep fault runs the next batch too.
poles: treat the bath as the suspect and remediate chemistry
run the prep-first diagnosis ladder before touching any bath
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the ladder is mandatory order: prep signatures are checked and cleared first because they are cheap to inspect and statistically dominant, and bath work begins only when the ladder exonerates the chain

edge_cases.description: A piece passes the water-break test yet later peels with an organic signature at the interface
edge_cases.trigger: surfactant drag-out from a fresh, heavily wetted cleaner sheets over remaining soil and fakes a pass
edge_cases.mitigation: read the gate only after honest warm rinsing, re-rinse and re-read suspicious passes from fresh cleaner, and treat any organic-signature failure as impeaching that day's gate reads

edge_cases.description: Orange bloom appears on steel findings between the activation dip and the tank
edge_cases.trigger: a transfer delay - a phone call, a dropped rack, a long walk - lets activated steel flash-rust in air
edge_cases.mitigation: the bloom is a mandatory loop-back through activation, never plated over; recurrence drives the layout fix of shortening the dip-to-tank path and cutting batch size

edge_cases.description: A zinc die-cast piece froths and pits within seconds of touching a standard acid tank
edge_cases.trigger: a die-cast piece routed down a copper-alloy or steel branch because appearance overruled the docket, or the docket was wrong
edge_cases.mitigation: pull the piece immediately, stop the line, document the damage honestly for the customer conversation, and audit how the wrong branch was entered before running the next piece

edge_cases.description: A refinish job over old nickel plate keeps shedding its new gold despite perfect gate passes
edge_cases.trigger: the aged nickel surface is passive, and ordinary activation cannot defeat a self-healing film
edge_cases.mitigation: reclassify previously plated work into the passive class on the map, route it through the live-entry strike handoff, and add the flag to the docket format so the next refinish arrives labeled

edge_cases.description: Work develops a hazy gel film in the pickle and later shows paint-like peeling
edge_cases.trigger: silicated cleaner drag-in polymerizing in acid because the post-soak rinse was skimped
edge_cases.mitigation: hot double rinse after any silicated cleaner or switch to a low-silicate product per TDS, and treat gel in the pickle as evidence the rinse stage between them is under-designed

edge_cases.description: The ultrasonic opens a solder seam on a piece whose docket carried no repair flag
edge_cases.trigger: a hidden starved repair joint that assessment could not see and the docket therefore missed
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the cycle at the first rattle or visible movement, return the piece to assessment with the observation, and amend the docket fields so comparable construction is flagged in future

edge_cases.description: A steel clasp electrocleaned in cathodic mode passes every visual check and peels days later
edge_cases.trigger: polarity set by plating habit (work as cathode) plates smut onto the surface that only time reveals
edge_cases.mitigation: make lead polarity a checked item against the substrate class before current flows, and when late peel appears on steel, put polarity at the top of the diagnosis ladder

edge_cases.description: Spotting appears on plated work though every prep step ran normally
edge_cases.trigger: the final rinse quietly degraded - an exhausted DI cartridge or a tap-water top-up nobody logged
edge_cases.mitigation: audit with the conductivity pen from make-up water forward, restore the water grade, and move pen readings from on-suspicion to a fixed cadence

edge_cases.description: An operator instinctively steadies a gate-passed pendant with a bare thumb during transfer
edge_cases.trigger: a swinging or slipping piece and the reflex to catch it faster than the rule can intervene
edge_cases.mitigation: the touch is confessed and the piece re-runs from soak - a wipe is not recovery - and the rack design that made the piece swing gets fixed so the reflex is not invited again

edge_cases.description: A hollow charm carries trapped cleaner through every later tank and weeps it out in the gold
edge_cases.trigger: cupped geometry racked mouth-up, holding a hidden reservoir through drain dwells that empty everything else
edge_cases.mitigation: orient hollow geometry to drain at racking, add a tip-and-drain motion at each transfer for known trap shapes, and route pieces whose geometry cannot drain back to assessment for a venting decision

edge_cases.description: The soak cleaner collapses mid-batch and half the load fails the gate
edge_cases.trigger: solution exhaustion crossing its threshold inside one batch after weeks of slow drift the log would have shown
edge_cases.mitigation: remake the cleaner per TDS, re-run the entire batch from soak including the pieces that passed, and tighten the control-test cadence that let the drift go unread

edge_cases.description: The rectifier dies mid-electroclean and the load sits in hot alkaline solution without current
edge_cases.trigger: equipment failure or a tripped circuit during the electroclean cycle
edge_cases.mitigation: remove and rinse the load, treat the interrupted cycle as void rather than resumable, and restart cleaning from the soak with a fresh gate read once current is restored

workflow.action: Check the triage docket against the piece in hand
workflow.description: Confirm substrate class, flag status, and sign-off state are complete, current, and match the physical piece
workflow.artifact: verified docket attached to the job
workflow.gate: no docket or any mismatch refuses the piece back to assessment before any immersion
